Subject: Recap + Next Steps: POC trial planning (AcmeHealth)

Hi Alice / Jamal — thanks again for your time this morning. Quick recap from our discovery and proposed next steps to kick off the POC trial: 

Summary of goals / success criteria:
- Validate latency SLO: 95th pctile inference latency <= 250ms for 512-token requests.
- Cost target: < $0.0008 per token in production configuration (target to evaluate savings from batching + quantization).
- Quality: answer accuracy on clinical triage prompts >= 92% vs your gold set.

Evaluation plan / timeline:
- Week 0 (this week): finalize workload intake and success criteria, sign mutual action plan.
- Week 1: provision POC instance (dedicated tenant), ingest sample dataset, run baseline tests.
- Week 2: tuning (batching/quantization), run evaluation harness and perf/load tests.
- Week 3: review results, recommendations for production sizing or Dedicated reservation.

Workload intake items we need from you (details below are ideal to complete provisioning):
- Typical RPS and peak RPS (per endpoint)
- Average and 95th token lengths for prompts and responses
- Concurrent users / concurrency targets and burst patterns (hourly/daily)
- Any request size limits or multi-turn context lengths (max context tokens)

Ownership / contacts:
- Redwood SE: Marissa Cole (technical lead for provisioning and tests)
- Redwood AE: Ben Carter (program lead / commercial)
- AcmeHealth Eng: Jamal Ortiz (POC owner) and Alice Nguyen (clinical/product)

Deliverables attached: initial POC plan (RDW-Acme-POC-Plan-20270515.pdf). Can you confirm the success criteria above and send workload numbers? If you’re good, we’ll send the mutual action plan for signature and schedule the provisioning window (we can start as early as Monday).

Thanks — Ben

Ben Carter

Thanks Ben — appreciate the clear plan. Confirming the success criteria look right from our side. Below are the workload numbers you requested (high level) — I attached a short spreadsheet with per-endpoint breakdown.

Workload summary (prod-like estimates):
- Endpoints: clinical-triage (primary), summarization (secondary)
- Typical RPS: 12 RPS aggregate (clinical-triage: 9 RPS, summarization: 3 RPS)
- Peak RPS (sustained 10m window): 75 RPS (burst windows during rounding)
- Concurrency target: 60 concurrent requests (mostly short-lived HTTP requests)
- Prompt token lengths (avg / 95th): clinical-triage prompts 120 / 420 tokens; responses avg 180 / 640 tokens
- Summarization prompts 300 / 1200; responses 400 / 1600
- Max context window: 4,096 tokens
- Typical request pattern: steady baseline during day (8am-6pm) with spikes at 9am and 2pm for ~8-12 minutes

We have a small subset (2k anonymized conversations) we can share for evaluation; Jamal will coordinate secure upload. We prefer Dedicated tenant for isolation but open to starting on a private demo instance first.

-Alice

Product Lead, Clinical AI | AcmeHealth

Great details — thanks Alice. A few quick technical follow-ups so we size the POC correctly: 

1) For the 75 RPS peak (10m), is that mostly parallel short requests or are there bursts where a single request stays open for long streaming? My guess is short (non-streaming) HTTP requests but please confirm.
2) For the long summarization responses (up to 1600 tokens), do you expect multi-turn contexts to include past generated tokens or just the last user note + patient data? We need to know for KV cache sizing.
3) Any encryption/HIPAA constraints for the dataset upload? If so we'll provide a presigned S3 with a time-limited token and an NDA/procurement contact.

I'll draft a quick perf matrix: baseline (no quant, minimal batching), tuned batch/quantized, and a misc configuration for streaming vs non-streaming so we can compare latency and cost numbers.

If you confirm 1-3 we can lock in provisioning for Monday morning.

Thanks — Marissa

Marissa Cole
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com
From: Jamal Ortiz <jamal.ortiz@acmehealth.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Cc: Alice Nguyen <alice.nguyen@acmehealth.com>
Date: Sat, 15 May 2027 13:42:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Recap + Next Steps: POC trial planning (AcmeHealth)

Marissa — answers below: 
1) Peak bursts are parallel short requests (no streaming) — clinicians submit short payloads and expect a synchronous reply. Occasionally a user will trigger a longer summarization job but those are background and can tolerate higher latency.
2) Multi-turn context: for clinical-triage we send the last 2 messages plus patient metadata, so effective context is generally <= 800 tokens. For summarization we may pass in up to 3 prior notes, pushing context toward 3,000 tokens in rare cases.
3) HIPAA: yes — dataset upload needs to use our S3 with customer-managed keys. We have an internal procurement NDA; procurement@acmehealth.com can coordinate.

We'll upload the anonymized sample by EOD Monday and Jamal will share access details. Looking forward to the perf matrix.

— Jamal
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Alice Nguyen <alice.nguyen@acmehealth.com>, Jamal Ortiz <jamal.ortiz@acmehealth.com>

- SE deliverables: baseline perf report (no quant) and a tuned config (intelligent batching + 4-bit quant) with expected cost/latency projections by EOW.

Thanks — Ben
